LESSON: LISTENING

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: Effective Communication By the end of the sub-strand,  Learners share their exp
Topic 1.1: LISTENING

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on LISTENING. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What do we talk a) listen attentively and to the theme my home about?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. recognize and use pronunciation, turn taking skills, in vocabulary related to the pairs and small groups themes myself, my family, 

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LISTENING
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
LISTENING helps you succeed in LITERACY ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: LISTENING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Recognize and use pronunciation, turn taking skills, in vocabulary related to the pairs and small groups themes myself, my family, 

What this means
In this part you learn to recognize and use pronunciation, turn taking skills, in vocabulary related to the pairs and small groups themes myself, my family, . You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognize and use pronunciation, turn taking skills, in vocabulary related to the pairs and small groups themes myself, my family, .
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “LISTENING”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognize and use pronunciation, turn taking skills, in vocabulary related to the pairs and small groups themes myself, my family, . Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what LISTENING is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “LISTENING”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: recognize and use pronunciation, turn taking skills, in vocabulary related to the pairs and small groups themes myself, my family, )

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach LISTENING to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: recognize and use pronunciation, turn taking skills, in vocabulary related to the pairs and small groups themes myself, my family, .
3. Make one local Kenya example of LISTENING from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for LISTENING: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 1 learner study LISTENING?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What do we talk a) listen attentively and to the theme my home about?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what LISTENING means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: recognize and use pronunciation, turn taking skills, in vocabulary related to the pairs and small groups themes myself, my family, .

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
